Encoding of phased genotypes in a gen_tibble

Source: R/phased_genotypes.R
phased_encoding.Rd

Phased diploid genotypes (read with phased = TRUE in gen_tibble()) are stored in the same file backed matrix (a bigstatsr::FBM.code256) as unphased ones, using one byte per genotype:

Usage

code_phased

phased_bytes

Format

code_phased is a numeric vector of length 256. phased_bytes is an integer matrix with 256 rows (bytes 0 to 255) and two columns (hap1 and hap2).

Details

bytegenotypedosage (code256)
00|00
10|11
21|12
3missingNA
41|01

Bytes 0 to 3 have the same meaning as in unphased diploid data (where byte 3 is the missing value), so that code that reads or writes the raw bytes keeps working; only the second orientation of a heterozygote (1|0) uses a new byte. The code256 of the matrix, code_phased, translates each byte into a dosage, so that all functions that decode genotypes through code256 see phased data as ordinary unphased dosages. code_phased is also how phased data are recognised (is_phased()): it differs from the codes used for unphased (bigsnpr::CODE_012), imputed (bigsnpr::CODE_IMPUTE_PRED) and dosage (bigsnpr::CODE_DOSAGE) data, as it is the only one that decodes byte 4 as 1.

phased_bytes gives, for each byte, the alleles carried by the first and second haplotype of an individual (NA for missing, and for bytes that are not used).

See also

gen_tibble(), is_phased(), show_haplotypes()

Examples

code_phased[1:6]
#> [1]  0  1  2 NA  1 NA
phased_bytes[1:6, ]
#>      hap1 hap2
#> [1,]    0    0
#> [2,]    0    1
#> [3,]    1    1
#> [4,]   NA   NA
#> [5,]    1    0
#> [6,]   NA   NA
